sentences.text: The key thing to understand about Andy Burnham's speech is these were the words and the delivery of both a new prime minister and a grieving son.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Burnham is living through two life-shaping, even life-defining moments right now – becoming and adjusting to being prime minister during the final weeks of his dad Roy's life, and preparing his speech while dealing with the grief of his loss.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: The funeral will take place in a few days' time.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Reflections on his dad's life and influence formed the personal spine to this deeply political speech, which ranged far and wide.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Labour figures are enthused that they now have a leader with what they see as a clear sense of purpose that can be easily articulated.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: The tacit, unflattering comparison with former PM Sir Keir Starmer is obvious .
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid What stood out in this speech was its breadth.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: His pitch could, very broadly, be divided into the short term - what he hopes to achieve before a general election; and the long term - the prospectus he is beginning to assemble to put to the country when polling day comes around inside the next three years.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: The biggest ideas have the longest timeframe and, perhaps, the greatest need for a lengthy debate in their gestation.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Take the headline grabber: revamping social care in England.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Previous attempts to do so, by both Labour and the Conservatives, haven't survived the intensity of a general election campaign, having been announced close to an election.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: The aim of Burnham's plan is to seed a conversation now about what a new system might look like – the idea being that the argument is won in advance.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: The debate is only just beginning.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: The plan to fund this by making increases in the state pension from 2030 less generous than they are now was more detailed than some expected at this stage.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: The triple lock means the state pension currently increases annually in line with inflation, average wage growth or 2.5%, whichever is highest.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: But from April 2030, if Labour win the next election, the annual earnings link will be dropped.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: It would, Labour figures say, be increased further if needed, to ensure that it stays above 30% of the full time average wage.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Knowing they would face blunt criticism about binning the existing triple lock – note the reaction of the Unite union and Labour's political rivals – it would appear the prime minister was keen to offer as much of what he hopes will be reassuring detail to many.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Also going into the next Labour manifesto, he said, a change in the Westminster voting system and – after a review to come – the idea of a closer relationship with the European Union.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: How much closer, with what trade offs and prompting what reaction, we don't yet know.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: And from the longer term stuff to the here and now – including housing reform in England, more public control of the water industry and the electricity grid.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: There was an energy and sense of urgency to Burnham's pitch and without question he has created a battalion of dividing lines with Labour's political opponents which are likely to dominate the debate ahead.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: His cabinet and many in his party are relishing the battle of ideas the prime minister has set up and is enthusiastically leaning into.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: It was noteworthy that beyond a broad reference to Labour's opponents on the Right, the party's rivals didn't get a mention in a speech lasting more than an hour.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: The question is: does he and his government have the capacity to deliver?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: And do they have the capacity to convince you, the voter, they have a vision you regard as coherent, appealing and affordable?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: You hardly need reminding of the backdrop that contributed to thwarting many of his recent, many predecessors: a persistently sclerotic economy and a persistently turbulent international picture, for starters.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Neither will make turning all of this into a reality straightforward.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Beetles that look as if they are gold plated are among the millions of specimens that will be available to view online Researchers are using AI to create a vast digital museum of millions of specimens from collections across the UK that they say could "supercharge" our understanding of the natural world.

sentences.text: The new digital museum will enable researchers to understand how the UK has changed over the entire history of our planet and predict future changes to the climate, food supplies and species loss.

sentences.article_title: How AI is creating a UK super-museum and revealing our planet's history

sentences.article_title: How AI is creating a UK super-museum and revealing our planet's history

sentences.text: Chinese AI developer Moonshot is conducting an internal review after researchers were able to persuade two of its popular Kimi models to tell them how to make biological weapons and carry out assassinations.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Mindgard, which tests the security of AI systems, told the BBC it discovered in July that Kimi K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade safety limits put in place by developers.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: It arose during a process called "jailbreaking", where researchers use a series of complex instructions to see if AI tools ignore guardrails - which Mindgard said should have stopped Kimi from discussing concerning topics.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Moonshot told the BBC it welcomed third-party input "as a key pillar for building better and safer AI".
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: The company also told the BBC it was in discussion with Mindgard about its findings.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Mindgard's founder Peter Garraghan told the BBC World Service programme Tech Life that its findings about Kimi K2.6 and K3 Swarm were concerning.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: "Once the jailbreak works it will talk about any topic, it will even freely offer up recommendations about other topics that are also nefarious and it will be inventive and creative," he said.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Jailbreaks present a different kind of risk to those seen with the recent slew of high-profile AI incidents .
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: These have seen autonomous AI tools known as agents, developed by US firms including OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic, hack some online services.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: While jailbreaks are complex processes that can take a lot of time and determination some experts fear hackers and other bad actors could try to use them to cause harm.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Anthropic recently said it had identified and disrupted attempts to use one of its AI model for "malicious activity" that could support the development of biological weapons .
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Mindgard has not proven whether the answers supplied by Kimi on concerning topics would work.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: But it argued guardrails should have prevented the models in question from entering into discussion with users on such subjects.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: The firm said it was also confident a jailbroken Kimi 2.6 could allow hackers to run code on its computing resources and connect to the internet - making it a potential launchpad for cyber-attacks.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Garraghan defended Mindgard's decision to publicly discuss its jailbreak of Moonshot's systems, saying it had informed the developer and was not revealing key details about how it got the firm's models to ignore guardrails.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Mindgard alerted Moonshot to the jailbreak in an email on 27 July, following up about a week later.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: It then published a blog about the issue on 12 September.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: But the company said Moonshot only made contact recently, after it was approached by the BBC for comment.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: In part of an email to Mindgard asking for more details, shared with the BBC by Moonshot, it said its model had generally shown  "a high refusal rate for these types of requests" in internal evaluations.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: The findings come as the AI industry continues to be split on whether closed, proprietary models - like those powering ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude systems - or open-source tools are the best or safest way forward.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Kimi is an open-weight model, meaning someone could in theory take the model and run it themselves on their own computing infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Prof Alan Woodward, of the University of Surrey, told the BBC there was a risk open-source models might end up in the wrong hands, but they could also be harnessed for cyber-defence.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

Like Mindgard founder Garraghan, Prof Woodward believes there should be a greater focus on identifying and prosecuting humans who misuse AI.

sentences.text: Six Flags Magic Mountain, an amusement park in California, has announced it will permanently close a popular rollercoaster after hundreds of riders alleged they suffered brain injuries.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: The X2 rollercoaster, one of the park's main attractions, with long wait times to ride and seats that spin 360 degrees, has been closed since July.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: Six Flags said the ride had passed a range of safety tests, but that it had decided to retire it because it was "the right thing to do".
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: The decision comes after lawsuits and news reports alleged that hundreds of riders suffered brain injuries after riding X2.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: A law firm representing some of the plaintiffs said the decision had come "too late" for its clients.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: "They got on X2 expecting a thrill.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: Instead, they left with catastrophic brain injuries," the firm said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: "Some needed emergency brain surgery.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: Some are still fighting to get their lives back." The law firm said that while it welcomed the closure of the ride to protect future guests, "it does nothing for the people who have already been hurt".
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: Originally called X, the ride first opened in 2002 but was closed months later for repairs to design flaws, the Los Angeles Times reports.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: It was then closed again in 2007 to replace its trains with lighter versions.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: It reopened the following year as X2 and since then has been ridden by more than 16 million people, the park said.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: A law firm that represented the family of 22-year-old Christopher Hawley, who died after riding X2 in 2022, said the closure was not enough.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: While the Hawley family is "relieved to hear that Six Flags is finally closing the X2, it does not change the fact that Christopher Hawley was killed by a dangerous roller coaster that was allowed to operate for nearly two decades," attorney Brent Wisner of Wisner Baum LLP said in a statement to the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: Hawley's family settled a wrongful death suit with the theme park in August.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: "That tragedy cannot be undone," Wisner said, calling for legal reform, proactive regulation and proper governmental oversight.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: "We cannot rely on profit-centered corporations to do the right thing only after enough people have been hurt," he added.
sentences.article_title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after hundreds allege brain injuries

sentences.text: "We hope that whatever replaces the X2 is safe."

sentences.text: Trump met with top tech leaders at the White House on Tuesday to discuss AI US President Donald Trump hosted a meeting of top technology bosses on Tuesday for what he called "an extraordinary gathering" of the minds that are "building America's Golden Age".
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The guest list included leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, Meta and Google - all key figures in the US AI industry.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The meeting came as some tech executives and experts have called for tighter oversight of AI and a slowdown in developing the technology, citing concerns about the potential risks it poses to humanity.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Here are three key takeaways from Trump's tech summit at the White House.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Trump took questions from the media for around 30 minutes alongside House Speaker Mike Johnson and top tech leaders after the closed-door meeting.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The president told reporters that the executives had signed a "morally binding" document that would serve as a "form of protection" from AI's potential risks.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Under the agreement, which Trump posted on social media, the companies are responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The firms also agreed to implement safeguards to keep models operating as intended and quickly detect and fix any issues, the document said.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "It's almost like a constitution, in a way," Trump said, referring to the agreement.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "And the biggest people in the world signed that, and I signed it as president." Trump with top tech leaders at the White House on Tuesday Trump added that he will set up a board to oversee the safety of AI tools.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: He did not specify who would be on that board.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The president has repeatedly downplayed concerns about AI's risks, dismissing them as a "hoax".
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: He has said the only "guardrails" the industry needs is a "smart" president.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: OpenAI and Anthropic have in recent weeks called for tighter oversight  of the industry and foe a slowdown of development of the technology.

sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Trump also reiterated his support for the rapid expansion of data centres - the crucial computing infrastructure that powers AI.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The rollout of data centres has drawn pushback around the country over concerns about electricity usage and their potential impact on from communities.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Data centre construction has also emerged as a potential political obstacle for Trump's Republican party ahead of the US midterm elections in November.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: A survey conducted by Marist Poll in partnership with NPR and PBS News , external earlier this month found that 65% of registered voters opposed data centres being built in their areas.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Responding to those concerns, Trump said tech companies would work to make people "happy" about the construction of data centres.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "These big, powerful, very rich, very smart companies are going to be making massive contributions to communities," Trump told reporters.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Trump previously said on social media that the only reason communities in the US should oppose data centres is if they "want to end up being backwards and poor".
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "The good news is that there are plenty of other places that want them.

sentences.text: If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame," he said.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: A delegation of BAPS Hindu monks visited the Eiffel Tower as part of a visit to Paris to open a new temple earlier this month The chief executive of the company that runs the Eiffel Tower will step down after a backlash over female staff being replaced by male colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group.

sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.text: Australia and China have had diplomatic relations since 1972 but it was only in the early 2010s that China became Australia's biggest trading partner, hungry for all the commodities it had to offer.
sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.text: Australia opened up its economy and encouraged business and trade, Chinese President Xi Jinping was invited to address parliament.
sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.text: The golden era didn't last long though.
sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.text: When Australia suggested an investigation into the origins of Covid in 2020, China objected to this line of questioning and retaliated with tariffs.
sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.text: A number of Australians have also been detained in China, including journalist Cheng Lei, who was released in 2023 after more than three years.
sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.text: China is Australia's biggest export market Even with these hiccups, this year's Lowy Institute Poll found that a majority of Australians (61%) saw China more as an economic partner than a security threat.

sentences.text: That was an 11-point increase from last year.
sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.text: When it comes to China investing in Australia though, they are more wary.
sentences.article_title: The Frenemy: How Australia navigates superpower rivalry

sentences.text: This video can not be played The journalist who became king Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma has been crowned king of Uganda's Tooro kingdom.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The new monarch has long been a familiar face in the East African nation, where for many he was known not as the heir to the throne, but as a storyteller: a long-serving anchor and editor at the state broadcaster.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: But the 56-year-old - now King Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Nyabongo I - has become the subject of media attention himself as his rise to the Tooro throne sparked controversy and widespread reactions beyond the country.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Tooro is one of Uganda's four main officially recognised historical kingdoms.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: For the last 31 years, it had been headed by King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who was once known as a "boy king", after ascending to the throne as an infant.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Oyo became king in 1995 at the age of just three, following the death of his father.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Then the world's youngest monarch, he ruled until he died last month from cancer, aged just 34.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The coronation is a day for celebration, involving traditional practices that started at midnight.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma has had to perform various ceremonies and walk about 4km (2.5 miles) to the official Karuziika royal palace where he has now been crowned.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The Tooro kingdom's Information Minister Charles Mwanguhya told the BBC Focus on Africa podcast that a mock fight would follow his crowning, to signify that kingship does not come easy.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma would then be blessed by members of the royal Babiito clan, he said.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: But his selection was far from straightforward.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: According to tradition, a recognised son of the late king should have succeeded him.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Close members of the royal family said Oyo had left a young son and a will with instructions that the child should be next on the throne.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: But the son has never been revealed to the public and nor was he recognised by the committee of 21 Babiito clan members who choose the king and eventually selected Kijanangoma.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The late King Oyo was never publicly married, and little is known about his wife or their son.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Nonetheless his mother, Queen Best Kemigisa, argued that the late king's will ought to have been respected.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: However, the royal succession committee ignored her wishes, insisting their selection process was conducted in accordance with Tooro customs and traditions.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The new king has thus found himself at the centre of a succession dispute, with Kemigisa and her close relatives unhappy with the outcome.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The late King Oyo's mother has expressed her pain over the succession row Kemigisa referred to Kijanangoma's selection as the "announcement of a second king" being "made after the will of King Oyo was read to members of the royal family".
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: "As a mother, that was extraordinarily painful," she said, describing celebrations for the next king taking place "only metres from where my son's body lay".
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The queen later said Oyo's son, who was in the US state of Texas, had been due to return home but that could not happen amid a "tense and polarised succession dispute".
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: "No child should be placed in circumstances where returning to his father's homeland could mean being drawn into hostility and conflict," Kemigisa asserted in a post on X.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: But according to the Tooro kingdom's information minister, the son being talked about "hasn't been presented anywhere, which means there is a growing acceptance that sad as it may be, King Oyo didn't leave a son behind".
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: While King Oyo inherited the crown from his father, Mwanguhya told the BBC "the crown has moved to a different line within the ruling clan".
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma and the late King Oyo are cousins.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: After he was formally announced, Kijanangoma promised that the palace would be open to the people, while vowing to focus on unity and development.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: "I ask you for one thing - they have given me this title as king but I cannot work alone, I have to work with you," he said.

sentences.text: President Museveni (left), who restored the traditional kingdoms in the 1990s, was pictured with Tooro's King Oyo (right) in 2010 Uganda's traditional kings have no formal political authority, but they retain cultural influence and command significant loyalty in the communities they lead.

sentences.text: The country is home to four main kingdoms, the largest and most prominent being Buganda in the central region, which encompasses the capital Kampala.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The government said this was to promote cultural pride and national unity, but the move has also been interpreted as a way of appeasing communities and fostering political loyalty.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: His father, the first Kijanangoma, was born in the year King Rukidi III became king.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: The king gave him the name, which means the "one who comes with the royal drum".
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma was born in 1970 and raised at their family home at Kidukuru village in Fort Portal, about 300km (186 miles) from Kampala.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: He left the village to pursue further studies and graduated with a mass communication degree from Uganda's prestigious Makerere University in 1999.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: He worked as a broadcaster in a career spanning more than two decades, including in neighbouring Rwanda and at home, with the Uganda Broadcasting Corporation (UBC).
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: Kijanangoma has been a journalist for much of his adult life The years spent engaging with the public, the interactions with leaders and the exposure to national affairs in his work as a journalist may yet serve him well as he returns to the community he came from, this time as their leader.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: After he was named king, Kijanangoma said he would use the connections he had built up over 21 years working as a journalist "to get good things for our people".
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: His mother, Assimwe Yusta Kijanangoma, is confident that he is well prepared for his new role.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: She says his upbringing was deeply rooted in tradition.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: "I really raised him with the teachings of the old kingdom of a cane and instructions and scolding.
sentences.article_title: Journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute

sentences.text: PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough were killed in the collision No evidence of "tactical contact" or the use of a stinger has been found before the A66 crash which killed five young men and two police officers, an initial investigation has revealed.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: The crash between a Volkswagen Passat and a marked Cleveland Police vehicle happened at South Bank, near Middlesbrough, on 22 August and followed a police pursuit which was abandoned.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: The initial investigation by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said there was no evidence police had initiated contact with the Passat.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: However, director of engagement, Emily Barry, said it will take the IOPC months to conclude its full investigation due to the amount of information to review.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, who had not been following the Passat, were killed.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: The five people in the Passat were Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jakub Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, and 17-year-olds Theo Rae and Cole Robert Worthy.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: The five who died in the Passat were Jakub Matusiak, Makai Saddington, Theo Rae, Michael Robert Cahill and Cole Robert Worthy The IOPC said the pursuit began at 03.33 BST and six minutes and 12 seconds later, the Passat slowed as it approached the A66, turned right and headed the wrong way down the dual carriageway.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: The pursuing police driver did not follow the Passat along the wrong carriageway, turned off the blue warning lights and headed along the A66 on the right side of the road, the watchdog said.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: The Passat collided with the car PC Clough and PC Blades were in around 17 seconds later.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: A forensic collision investigator is still working to ascertain the speed of both vehicles at the point of collision.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: Barry said: "We continue to recognise the devastating and long-lasting impact this incident has had on the families and those in the force, the policing community, and the wider local community.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: "We are aware there is speculation regarding how the collision occurred.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: "There is no suggestion the collision was a result of any direct police contact, nor was a stinger used by the police in an attempt to stop the Passat." A stinger is a portable spike strip used to puncture the tyres of a vehicle.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: The IOPC has commissioned two expert reports, with one considering the collision reconstruction and another assessing the relevant policies and procedures that are in place for officers during pursuits.
sentences.article_title: No 'deliberate' contact to stop car in A66 crash

sentences.text: Daniel Thomas, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, appeared in court via videolink (file photo) Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has been refused bail during a crown court hearing over the alleged slashing of a dinghy in the English Channel.
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas refused bail over alleged boat damage

sentences.text: Thomas, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, appeared via videolink at Portsmouth Crown Court accused of criminal damage after a video appeared to show him slashing at the boat with a knife.
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas refused bail over alleged boat damage

sentences.text: The 37-year-old, whose address was withheld by the court at a previous hearing, is also charged with failing to disclose the PIN to his phone.
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas refused bail over alleged boat damage

sentences.text: He has been remanded in custody, with a provisional trial date set for 1 March.
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas refused bail over alleged boat damage

sentences.text: The defendant, wearing a grey t-shirt and holding a copy of the Bible, did not enter a plea during the hearing but previously pleaded not guilty to both charges at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas refused bail over alleged boat damage

sentences.text: He is accused of slashing a boat that had been used by migrants, which was adrift in the sea, while a rescue crew member was on board.
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas refused bail over alleged boat damage

sentences.text: He is also alleged to have said "this is what needs to happen" and "this is England, this isn't France any more".
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas refused bail over alleged boat damage

sentences.text: Simon Pentol KC, defending, had proposed a "package of bail conditions" as an alternative to Thomas being remanded in custody and described the allegation against his client as "politically charged and fundamentally flawed".
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas refused bail over alleged boat damage

sentences.text: On his decision to refuse bail, the Judge James Newton-Price KC, said: "I am not concerned with the political issues or motivations in this matter and I put them aside in deciding this matter." A handful of supporters waited outside the court to hear the outcome of the hearing.
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas refused bail over alleged boat damage

sentences.text: Vickrum Digwa was jailed for life with a minimum of 21 years for Henry Nowak's murder The man who murdered student Henry Nowak is being allowed to appeal against the length of his sentence.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: Vickrum Digwa stabbed 18-year-old Henry Nowak to death in Southampton in December 2025.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: In June, he was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: He has now been given permission to challenge the length of that sentence at the Court of Appeal on 5 November.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: The court will also decide on a referral by the Attorney General's office, which argued the sentence was too lenient.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: Digwa has also applied to appeal against his conviction for murder, which will be decided separately.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: The 23-year-old was also sentenced for possessing a knife in public, despite claiming in court that the 21cm (8in) blade was being carried as part of his Sikh faith.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: Henry Nowak was a student at the University of Southampton After stabbing Nowak, who came from Chafford Hundred in Essex, Digwa lied to police that he was the victim of a racist attack.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: The case later sparked protests after police body-worn footage was released showing officers failing to give Nowak first aid and instead handcuffing him as he lay dying, despite him telling officers he could not breathe.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: The Independent Office for Police Conduct previously said it was investigating two officers for potential gross misconduct.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: Twelve police officers and a police dog were injured during the protests in Southampton on 2 June.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: Demonstrators gathered outside the city centre police station before moving to an area near the Digwa family home and the murder scene.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: More than 30 people have so far been charged with violent disorder following the incident.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: On 15 June, former Solicitor General Ellie Reeves KC referred the case to the Court of Appeal under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: Sikh leaders have reported a "backlash" and increase in "hate crime" against their community following the case.
sentences.article_title: Nowak killer given leave to appeal against sentence

sentences.text: Angela Rayner took aim at the 'injustice' of leasehold in her conference speech Leaseholders will be given extra protections from "cowboy" property agents and hidden fees, Angela Rayner has announced.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The housing secretary told Labour's annual conference the government would legislate for a new independent regulator and launch a consultation to cap "rip off" administrative fees.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The changes would cover the estimated five million leaseholders in England and Wales who can be forced to pay a landlord for simple changes to their home, despite having bought it.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner told party activists she had heard of leaseholders being charged £250 for permission to own a pet and £400 to change their front door.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She said people in these situations were "powerless against the vested interests that only take, while giving nothing back in return".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government is already legislating , external to ban new leasehold flats, described in Labour's 2024 election manifesto as a "feudal" system where people own the right to occupy a property via a lease for a limited number of years from a freeholder, or landlord, who owns the land.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Through the Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill , ministers want a commonhold system where residents collectively own and manage their buildings.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Now, Rayner is taking aim at the web of management companies that operate between leaseholders and their effective landlords.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She said the sector had many decent businesses which were "undermined by far too many cowboys, crooks and con artists".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: People excited at buying their own homes are "tricked" into using in-house services, meaning that "with no transparency or accountability, vultures can take advantage", Rayner added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: "We will legislate for an independent regulation to rein these cowboys in," she said, announcing legislation for an independent watchdog of property agents.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: This includes estate agents, managing agents and estate managers.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: This regulator would be able to set codes of practice, such as standards of conduct and proper complaint handling for those they regulate, and property agents will be required to obtain a licence.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: If they fall foul of the required standards, the regulator would have the power to take their licenses away, the government added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government said it wanted to bring forward the changes "as soon as possible".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner also said new legislation would create the power for caps on permission and administration fees leaseholders pay to landlords.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: These caps would cover freehold estates and privately managed estates where people can face additional fees for making cosmetic changes to their properties and requesting documents like building safety certificates.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: A public consultation will be launched to help decide the rate of caps.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: It comes in addition to an already-announced £250 cap on yearly ground rents paid by leaseholders in England and Wales, which had stalled during the change of prime minister over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government has said it expects the limit on ground rents - an annual fee paid by leaseholders to their freeholder - to come into force in late 2028, but MPs have called for this to be brought forward to late 2027.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner said she was "capping and then scrapping" ground rents, indicating she may try to go further than a cap.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: In her speech, Rayner did not mention the government's housing target of building 1.5m homes in England by the next election.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She admitted earlier this month there was only a "slim chance" of hitting it .
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Last week, ministers announced a new Your First Home policy to help first-time homebuyers in England with a deposit of 2.5%, similar to the Help To Buy scheme introduced under the Conservatives in 2013.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner also said she plans to strengthen council powers to take over empty homes to meet the need for council houses and tackle homelessness.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: But this was criticised by the Tories as a "desperate" attempt by Labour to try to hit its housing target.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Graeme Dott was sentenced to seven years in jail at the High Court in Edinburgh Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been jailed for seven years after being convicted of child sexual abuse.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Judge Lord Harrower said Dott robbed his victims of "a significant part of their childhood" and said his behaviour bore the hallmarks of grooming.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Dott had denied two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010 but was found guilty following a trial at the High Court in Glasgow.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The 49-year-old Scot, who won the world snooker title in 2006, showed no emotion as he was sentenced, only nodding to someone in the public gallery as he was led away.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: This video can not be played Former snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for child sexual abuse Lord Harrower told the High Court in Edinburgh that each of Dott's victims were vulnerable for reasons beyond their age.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: He said Dott rewarded the victims with treats and disguised his abuse as being part of a game.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The former snooker champion was 16 or 17 when he abused the girl, who was about nine when her ordeal began.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Dott's abuse of the second victim - a boy aged about eight - began about 10 years later.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The court heard that he warned them they would not be believed if they told anyone about his actions.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: As it happened: Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott sentenced The judge added Dott's victims had experienced "overwhelming emotions of fear, shame and anger" as a result of the abuse, affecting their mental health into adulthood.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Dott's behaviour towards the children "involved a gross violation of trust".
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: As Lord Harrower addressed him, Dott repeatedly shook his head in apparent disbelief.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The judge added social work reports have deemed Dott poses a "below average risk of reoffending", but as he still maintains his innocence, Lord Harrower could not take into account any remorse from Dott.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Graeme Dott abused a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010 The court also heard that Dott has already been the subject of threats and has been moved within prison as a result.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Euan Dow, representing Dott, told the court the father-of-two was now separated from his wife but "continues to enjoy the support of his family and friends".
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: He added Dott suffers from "long-standing mental health issues" and that his personal and professional reputations had been destroyed.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The sentence of seven years has been backdated to 24 August, which is when the 49-year-old was remanded in custody.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: He will spend the rest of his life on the sex offenders register.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Procurator Fiscal Faye Cook, of the Crown Office, said: "Graeme Dott achieved success and public admiration but, in private, he exploited the trust of two children to abuse and coerce them.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: "Dott's criminal behaviour has been his downfall and he now faces the consequences of his actions." She added that "justice has no time limit" and encouraged any victims of historical abuse to report it.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Dott was found guilty after a trial at the High Court in Glasgow in August During the trial, the court heard that Dott had exposed himself and inappropriately touched a primary school girl in the 1990s and attacked a young boy between 2006 and 2010.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Dott called the allegations made against him "disgusting".
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The girl, now a woman in her 40s, said Dott had "caressed" her bottom while giving her a piggyback and that, on another occasion, he had exposed himself to her.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: On another occasion, she said Dott, of Glasgow, suggested she "take her trousers down" and lifted her top and began kissing her stomach after asking if she wanted to "play a guessing game".
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The  victim said Dott would kiss her, touch her inappropriately and carried out a sexual act that would, if committed now, amount to rape.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: She said she recalled the "smell" of creams Dott used for a skin condition after he kissed her and that the actions left her "shocked and scared".
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The court heard that Dott bought her a teddy bear with a love heart on it in the course of the abuse.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Police previously contacted Dott about the allegations in 2001, but no charges were brought.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The woman gave a new statement to police in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Dott won the world championship title in 2006 During his evidence, Dott's male victim said the abuse began shortly after Dott defeated Peter Ebdon to win his sole world title at The Crucible in Sheffield in 2006.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The boy, now a man in his 20s, said he was about eight years old when Dott molested him in a shower at a home in South Lanarkshire.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: He told the court that Dott "rewarded" him with crisps and fizzy drinks and once handed him a £50 note, only to accuse the boy of stealing it when his parents found out he had the money.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: He also said he was abused in a car on a number of occasions and "inappropriately touched" while Dott played online poker.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Dott was convicted of lewd and libidinous practices, which refer to any sexual crimes against children committed prior to 1 December 2010.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: The offence was abolished in 2009, but is still used for crimes carried out before then.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Following his conviction in August, the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association said it had permanently revoked Dott's membership with immediate effect.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Dott was previously suspended from all professional snooker activities on 9 April 2025 pending the outcome of his trial.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: He was subsequently relegated from the professional ranking list at the conclusion of the 2025/26 season.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Dott has two previous convictions for minor road traffic offences in 2013 and 2015.
sentences.article_title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years for child sex abuse

sentences.text: Sam Altman has spoken repeatedly in recent weeks about the risks posed by AI agents.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: OpenAI on Tuesday unveiled "dots," a new artificial intelligence (AI) assistant they say can proactively carry out tasks on a user's behalf.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: Dots, however, were pitched as brightly coloured cute cartoons meant to function as digital assistants for people with busy lives.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: The dots, Altman said, "can handle really anything you can think of." A glossy video was shown during the event, with people speaking to and naming animated versions of their "dots," then giving them various tasks, like building a website and booking afterschool activities for their children.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: Speaking about "my dot," Altman almost entirely eschewed referring to the tool as an agent, which has been in common use for years.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: AI agents are essentially AI chatbots that are programmed to operate somewhat autonomously.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: "You just give your dot a responsibility... and your dots will just get to work and keep working," Altman added.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: OpenAI's event on Tuesday took place as President Donald Trump held a White House lunch with tech leaders and House Speaker Mike Johnson.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: Trump repeated his belief that AI companies should regulate themselves.

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham is to introduce a new scheme to try to help people "who have given up hope of ever having a home to call their own" get on the property ladder.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: The "Your First Home" scheme would be open to first-time buyers in England with a deposit of 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: It would provide them with a loan worth 20% of their new build property's value to help pay for the purchase.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: On Sunday, the government also shared plans it said would make it simpler for councils to take over empty homes to provide housing for those in need.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: The announcements come as the prime minister prepares for his first Labour conference as leader.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: With the "Your First Home" scheme, which was first announced on Saturday, there would be an initial interest-free period for the equity loan - more details on how it would work are expected in next month's Budget.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: The Conservatives warned the policy would leave first-time buyers taking on more debt and risks "pushing up the price of new homes" - the prime minister said those who do not have support from the "bank of mum and dad" are among those who it would aim to help.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: Burnham said: "Too many young people are struggling with the cost of housing, with many giving up hope of ever having a home to call their own.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: "So we will step in to help more first-time buyers on to the housing ladder." The PM added he believes the scheme will give builders the "confidence to deliver the high-quality new homes the country needs".
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: Funding for the scheme is expected to come from reprioritising existing budgets, but housing developers will pay towards the running costs.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: Ministers have not yet confirmed whether there is an age restriction on the scheme, or a cap on the price on the value of the property.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: On Sunday morning, the government also announced plans to strengthen council powers to take over empty homes to meet the need for council houses.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: It would, Labour said, make it simpler for councils to bring some of the more than 300,000 empty dwellings into use for essential housing.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: The plans were unveiled by Housing Secretary Angela Rayner ahead of the party's conference in Liverpool.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: Conservative shadow minister for state housing and planning Gareth Bacon accused her of "desperately reaching for any lever she can find" to hit "Labour's 1.5 million homes target".
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: It expanded a previous scheme, known as FirstBuy, which was aimed solely at first-time buyers.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: Help to Buy initially enabled all purchasers to put down a 5% deposit on a newly built home, with a value of up to £600,000.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: Up to 20% of the cost of the home was funded by a shared equity loan, which was interest-free for the first five years.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: The first version of the programme was active until 2021.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: A second iteration of the scheme, which ran until 2023, restricted access to first-time buyers and applied regional-level price caps to the properties that could be bought.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: In its conclusion, the report noted Help to Buy was "effective in supporting people into home ownership in some areas, but did not remove affordability barriers for first-time buyers in areas that were already relatively expensive".
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: "Our analysis shows a well-designed scheme can make a meaningful difference for households struggling to get on to the property ladder," it added.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: Lam said: "Slapping another levy on developers risks pushing up the price of new homes too.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: "This is a colossal admission of failure.
sentences.article_title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

sentences.text: This Labour government is making homes harder to build, then asking buyers to borrow more to pay for them." Lam said the Conservatives want to scrap stamp duty, "back British house builders" and ensure that houses are "built in the places that people actually want to live".

sentences.text: Merseyside Police said more than 50 protesters had been arrested More than 50 demonstrators have been arrested outside the Labour Party conference in Liverpool during a protest in support of the banned Palestine Action group, police have said.
sentences.article_title: More than 50 arrested at Palestine Action support rally

sentences.text: More than 250 protesters sat outside the conference centre earlier, many holding home-made banners which read: "I support Palestine Action".
sentences.article_title: More than 50 arrested at Palestine Action support rally

sentences.text: Scores of police officers stood by before moving in to start making arrests, warning protesters they were illegally holding signs supporting a proscribed organisation.
sentences.article_title: More than 50 arrested at Palestine Action support rally

sentences.text: After asking them if they were going to continue to do so, officers led some of the protesters away, telling them they had been arrested under the Terrorism Act.

sentences.text: A force spokesperson said it respected everyone's rights to protest lawfully while also aiming to keep the peace and ensure public safety.
sentences.article_title: More than 50 arrested at Palestine Action support rally

sentences.text: The force said it made "detailed and co-ordinated plans ahead of such events to ensure it can apply this consistently, fairly and proportionately".
sentences.article_title: More than 50 arrested at Palestine Action support rally
