sentences.text: An emergency vaccination programme followed an outbreak in Kent A vaccination programme targeting one million teenagers and young adults is being launched, after concerns about the number of meningitis B infections.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Officials say the programme will help protect those at "highest immediate risk".
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Meningococcal disease can lead to life-threatening illness.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Teenager's family 'heartbroken' by meningitis death Meningitis B vaccine to be offered to a million young people Meningitis is an infection of the protective membranes that surround the brain and spinal cord.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It can affect anyone but is most common in babies, young children, teenagers and young adults.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It can be very serious if not treated quickly.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The cause of the infection - either certain bacteria or viruses - can be determined by tests.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis is rarer but more serious than viral meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It can lead to blood poisoning or sepsis, and can affect the brain.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: This acute, severe infection is known as invasive meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It means the infection has invaded the blood stream or brain linings.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Meningitis B, or MenB, is behind most cases of more severe meningococcal disease in the UK.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Cases happen every year - in 2024-2025, there were 378 cases of invasive meningococcal disease, according to official data.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Symptoms can develop suddenly and can include: a rash that doesn't fade when pressed with a glass sudden onset of high fever severe and worsening headache extreme sleepiness/difficulty waking Two vaccines protect against the main causes of meningitis and septicaemia.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MenACWY vaccine offers protection against four types of bacteria that can cause meningitis - meningococcal groups A, C, W and Y - and is offered to teenagers aged 14 years old.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Anyone who missed out can get it for free until their 25th birthday.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine helps protect against meningococcal group B bacteria and is recommended for babies aged eight weeks, followed by a second dose at 12 weeks and a booster at one year.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The vaccines do not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Meningitis can sometimes occur as a complication of some other infections, meaning several other vaccinations can also help protect people.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: A six-in-one vaccine given to young children - also known as the DTaP/IPV/Hib/Hep B vaccine - offers protection against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, hepatitis B, polio and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib).
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: A pneumococcal vaccine offers babies protection against serious infections caused by pneumococcal bacteria, including meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MMRV vaccine - which replaced the MMR vaccine in January 2026 - offers infants protection against measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MMR vaccine is free for anyone who missed getting it when they were younger, regardless of their age.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Generally, it takes a couple of weeks to get full protection from a vaccine and some require booster doses.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: That means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide very long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Additionally, one million young people are now being offered the MenB vaccine in a one-off, targeted programme this summer to help protect them.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: All Year 13 pupils - meaning those who could soon leave for university - and anyone under 25 who is starting university or residential further education for the first time this autumn, will be able to get two doses of the vaccine for free on the NHS.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Experts say this population is at higher risk of potentially catching meningitis B which can spread when people live together in shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Invasive meningococcal disease tend to peak in October to November each year, which further heightens the risk.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Some people carry the bacteria in their nose or throat without getting sick, but can spread it to others through the exchange of spit or saliva in coughs, sneezes and kissing, or by sharing vapes and drinks.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Close personal contact is necessary for spread to happen.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The infection can also be spread by someone with meningitis, although this is less common.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It's possible to get meningitis more than once.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The best way to stop the disease spreading is to give antibiotics to people who may have come into contact with it.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Vaccination can also provide some protection from future infection.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Anyone becoming unwell with symptoms of meningitis or sepsis should seek medical help urgently at the closest Accident and Emergency Department or by dialling 999.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Early treatment can be lifesaving.

sentences.text: Schools are "crying out" for guidance from government on how pupils and teachers can use AI safely and effectively, a new report has warned.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Sir Anthony Seldon, former head teacher and author on AI in education, says the technology is being used more and more frequently, but that its introduction has been "chaotic and anarchic".
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: His report calls for the government to roll out a national framework for adopting AI in education in England, including training teachers on how to use it, which schools should use to develop their own "AI strategies" by September next year.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: The government says its changes to the curriculum in England will give children digital skills and help them spot disinformation.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Sir Anthony's report, co-authored with venture capitalist Tim Bunting, says schools have not been prepared for AI's arrival.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Sir Anthony co-founded the group AI in Education, which was set up in 2023 to help educational institutions navigate AI safely.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: His report argues that getting a grip of AI requires the same level of national urgency as wars and epidemics, and requires a taskforce modelled on the one which helped to roll out the Covid vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: "Put simply, education has not kept pace with how – and how much – young people are already using AI, and that gap is starting to show up as a loss of perceived value in the institution itself," the report says.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Department for Education says ministers take the "significant opportunities and challenges" of AI "incredibly seriously".
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: As well as refreshing the curriculum in England, they say they are building new AI tutoring tools and introducing new vocational routes to get children into successful careers.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Some schools have already embedded AI into the curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Benjamin Barker, principal at King's Leadership Academy Wavertree, says he wants his students to learn how to use tools safely, while also developing their critical thinking skills.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: Student Emma, 12, says she uses AI for her robotics projects, as well as proof-reading her English homework, and believes more students should be taught how to use it responsibly.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: "AI is coming into the future.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: It's getting more advanced," she says.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: "There's no way we're going to completely pull back from it.
sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report But the new system has faced criticism since it was first proposed , with Perry's sister Prof Julia Waters saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT issued a claim in the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but this was rejected.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Nearly a year after it was fully rolled out, the NAHT said evidence from its members suggested the new system is having a detrimental impact on school leaders' mental health.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Testimonies seen by the BBC suggest head teachers are being left "overwhelmed" and "anxious", with the pressure caused by the inspections described as "intolerable".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Although the system had been changed with the intention of lowering the burden on school leaders, the testimonies say the inspection and assessment process had become "higher stakes than ever before".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Amanda Hulme, head teacher at Claypool Primary School in Bolton, said a recent inspection at her school had been "easily the most stressful experience" of her career.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "It was definitely damaging to my health and really quite distressing," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I couldn't sleep and it led to my blood pressure and pulse rate increasing.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Powell told LBC earlier this month that she took head teacher wellbeing "incredibly seriously" and that the system of accountability needed to be "supportive and understanding.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I'll continue the work that I do with head teachers, head teacher representatives and others to make sure that we get this Ofsted framework, but also the culture and the whole regime, right," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT said the results of a recent survey of its members suggested that the majority who responded felt that inspections had worsened in the past 12 months.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The union is now calling for inspections to pause to allow for a "fundamental review of how inspection works", drawing on examples from other nations.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: In Wales, the inspectorate Estyn has removed judgements such as "excellent" and "good" from its reports, instead summarising findings by highlighting a school's strengths and areas for improvement.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Northern Ireland's Education and Training Inspectorate (ETI) also uses narrative reports without grades.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Scotland's His Majesty's Inspectorate of Education (HIME) does use grades, but there has been a recent consultation on their use.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: NAHT general secretary Paul Whiteman said: "The clear theme emerging across all the feedback we have received is that this Ofsted framework is even more stressful than the one that preceded it.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "Ofsted exists to raise standards for children and to provide clear reporting to parents," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "We will continue to engage closely with trades unions – but we will also continue to grade schools." Have you been impacted by the issues discussed in this story?

sentences.text: University applicants in England will be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out, the government has said.

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The interest rate on those loans is the Retail Prices Index (RPI) measure of inflation plus up to 3% depending on earnings, and borrowers repay at a rate of 9% of everything they earn over a repayment threshold, which is meant to rise with inflation every year.

sentences.text: The loans are written off after 30 years.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: English pupils have pulled ahead of the rest of the UK in international reading, maths and science tests, new data suggests, with Scotland and Wales falling further behind.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) saw reading and maths scores slump in each UK nation except England, while all four saw an uptick in science, with that rise again most notable in England.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The latest Pisa report, which is published every three years, also warned of a worldwide decline in teenagers' reading skills.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Teenagers were losing the skills that "matter most in the age of AI", such as being able to critically evaluate information from different sources, it said.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The share of "hasty readers", who rush through texts to give quick, incorrect answers, has almost doubled between 2018 and 2025.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The report warned the fall was greatest in those from "relatively well off" families.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Run by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), the Pisa tests assess teenagers on their ability to solve problems, think critically and communicate, before asking them a wider range of questions about their education in a questionnaire.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Although the UK performed well overall, the rankings varied significantly again, with results showing England, where the curriculum is significantly different, pulling consistently ahead of Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: England's schools minister, Georgia Gould, said the government wanted to "build on" the positive results and "go further so all young people leave school with strong literacy and numeracy".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The 2025 Pisa tests were taken by a sample of 760,000 15-year-olds in 91 countries.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: In the UK, where education differs between the home nations, 15,566 students took the tests in 515 schools.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: In England, where it was recently announced that technical subjects would soon be available to students from age 14 , Gould held up high-performing Estonia as an example of where "academic excellence can go hand in hand with high-quality vocational routes".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: "Our reforms will build on England's strong academic foundations so future generations not only perform well, but feel connected to school and excited about where their education can take them," she added.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: But Laura Trott, England's shadow education secretary, said the country's successes were down to previous reforms, and accused the new government of trying to "sabotage" them.

sentences.text: As the tests last year were taken by 15-year-olds, the results there largely reflect learning under an old curriculum, which has recently been changed.

sentences.text: Anna Brychan, Wales' minister for education and Welsh language, said plans were in place to support schools, adding that the results "highlight our need to improve standards of reading and maths, as a priority".

sentences.text: Scotland's education secretary, Mairi McAllan, said the results showed "real strengths in Scottish education, as well as areas we're already working to improve".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: But Scottish Labour said results had "flatlined since 2022's historically poor results", while the Scottish Liberal Democrats said the education system under the SNP had "tumbled down the rankings, lagging behind England on every measure of performance".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Northern Ireland's education minister, Paul Givan, said pupils there had performed well by international standards, but that - like other countries - its education system was facing "significant challenges", adding that "there is much more work to do".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Overall, the Pisa tests provide the biggest global snapshot of education systems and an independent view of how teenagers are performing compared with their peers in other countries, so it is a relative measure.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Andreas Schleicher, director of education at the OECD, said reading was the "mother of all skills" and that the steep decline was a concern.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: He said children's ability to read complex texts had declined by the equivalent of "two school years" in the last decade.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Longer-term Pisa research suggested students who read longer books performed best, he added, as it helped them to learn to hold complex information in mind.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Schools like Meadow Park, in Coventry, are adopting a range of approaches to improve pupils' reading skills, including weekly book club discussions led by tutors.

sentences.text: Year 10 pupil Ampaabeng said the sessions have had a "really positive impact" on his reading since they were brought in a year ago.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The school has also invested in a wider range of books in the library, where reading for pleasure at lunchtime is encouraged.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: A mobile phone ban was introduced at the school two years ago to reduce distractions - an approach which is commended by the new report.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: "In a digital age, it's easier to pick up a phone than it is a book," head teacher Bernadette Pettman said.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: She said reading together had enabled the school to "break down that fear of reading" and that pupils had "absolutely embraced it".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Bernadette Pettman says the school tries to make reading fun with book clubs, creative writing sessions and visits from authors One of the other big changes in education, picked up in the OECD's report, is the use of AI.

sentences.text: Martine Barons who began lifting weights during lockdown is now a three-time world champion A 65-year-old grandmother has become a three-time world champion powerlifter after only starting the sport two and a half years ago.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Martine Barons, from Stratford-upon-Avon, said she began lifting weights during lockdown after listening to a seminar that said women going through menopause should run less and lift more.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Her colleague at the University of Warwick, who is also a personal trainer, then showed Barons how to deadlift, and spotted her potential.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons is now nicknamed The Deadlifting Grandma.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: On Monday, she won at the AWPC World Powerlifting Championships in the 65 to 85 age group, becoming a three-time world champion, after starting out entering competitions just for fun.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said she has seen a "huge change" in her physique and capabilities "I have seen such a huge change in my own physique and my capabilities – I am sure that my body is at least 20 years younger," she told BBC CWR.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "When they invited me to the British and European Championships, I thought, 'Well I have been invited it would be rude not to go', but who thought it would lead to this?
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said her journey, down to hard work and dedication over the past couple of years, has been "so exciting".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "I have learnt so much, I have met people all around the world, and it has been delightful," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: For women who want to get fit and improve their strength, Baron said there were lots of options, one route is to join a gym and develop a tailored programme with a coach.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Alternatively, Baron said those who prefer more privacy could "start really gently at home with some resistance bands and a programme".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: She added her powerlifting has led to having more capability on a day-to-day basis, along with now being able to touch her toes first thing in the morning.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "If I need to move furniture at home, I can do that, I can toss my grandchildren in the air, I can play games with them," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "My posture is better and I just feel more capable and more confident in everyday life".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Sara Kahsai wants all survivors of FGM to seek help and not suffer alone Sara Kahsai grew up in Sudan but moved to Birmingham, England, in 2022 after marrying a bus driver from the city.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But as she settled into married life and her new home, she was coming to terms with a life-changing discovery.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara realised she was a victim-survivor of Female Genital Mutiliation (FGM), a procedure she had endured as a young girl.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was floored by the revelation and, not least, the excruciating pain she was now beginning to fully understand.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "The shock was massive," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It made it difficult with my physical relationship with my husband - but he was very kind and very patient with me." Warning: This story contains descriptions of the practices involved in female genital mutilation Sara turned to the one person she knew must have orchestrated it - her mother - and asked her why.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It was the culture to do it for everybody," she said her mother, still living in Africa, told her.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When I spoke to my mum she was really upset and she apologised to me." FGM involves the partial or total removal of female genitalia for non-medical reasons, and is practiced in some parts of Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It also happens within some migrant communities in the UK, where it is illegal and treated as child abuse.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It is also against the law to take a girl abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Reasons include social acceptance, religion, misconceptions about hygiene and preserving a girl or woman's virginity.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The Home Office website cites World Health Organisation figures showing three million girls undergo some form , external of the procedure every year in Africa alone.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The mum received help for her FGM after she found out she was pregnant When Sara fell pregnant, she finally told health professionals she had endured FGM as a child.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was immediately referred to the specialist FGM Clinic, run by midwives at Birmingham Women's Hospital.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif deals with around 200 cases each year and says her job is to ensure the wellbeing of women and safeguard unborn children.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "Some types of female circumcision can affect the vaginal delivery," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: They offer deinfibulation - a procedure that can be carried out during pregnancy to separate fused tissue and enable safer births.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: What is FGM, where does it happen and why?
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Victim-survivors of FGM can also experience difficulty with urinating and menstruating, the midwife said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Women are more prone to infections and sepsis, and can suffer from severe and ongoing pain, as well having to deal with psychological trauma, anxiety and depression.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Many patients find it hard to talk to her about what's happened to them, Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It is very difficult, very emotional.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's very difficult for the woman to actually come forward and to come to the clinic, attend the clinic, and have a conversation with me as well," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I explain to them that I'm here to help and I try to explain to them what happened to them when they were a child." She said most women leave the clinic with a better understanding of how they have been affected and how they can take back control of their bodies.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "We talk about every part, what that part is there for and what's been removed and what cause for concern and what effect this will have for the rest of her life," Hanif said.

sentences.text: Counselling is also offered as well as information on how partners and husbands can support them.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif runs the FGM centre at Birmingham Women's Hospital In 2015, children's charity Barnardo's set up the National FGM Centre to help better protect women and girls.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It works to prevent FGM, raise awareness of it and support those affected.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But how it is delivered can vary between schools.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's also not mandatory for it to be taught in primary schools and they want to see that change.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "For us, a huge part of tackling FGM is prevention," Rohma Ullah, from the centre, said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Among improvements on the way are new guidelines to help identify girls at risk of being taken abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara wants to urge other women in a similar position to take immediate action.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I have a message to all ladies who've had FGM," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When they come to the UK it is different.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: There's help here - go to their GP, seek help, ask for help.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Many farmers rely on government payments to manage their land in more environmentally-friendly ways Thousands of farmers missed out on vital government funding after online applications for a £233m green scheme for the whole of England closed down in under six hours.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Farming and environmental groups condemned the race to secure the sustainable farming incentive (SFI) funding, with some comparing it to a "frantic" online scramble to secure Glastonbury or Oasis gig tickets.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The post-Brexit scheme, which replaced EU subsidies with payments for farmers to look after nature and provide "public goods", opened at 10:00 BST on Tuesday but had run out of budget by 15:48 BST.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The government said farmers had responded "in force" to the scheme and there would be further funding opportunities for 2027.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The SFI scheme had been shut without warning last year so demand from farmers was expected to be high The National Farmers' Union (NFU) is calling for the government to explain why the scheme opened and closed so quickly, with so many farmers left out of pocket.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: It said it wanted "clarity and urgency" from the government and added that it had made "repeated warnings of a lack of sufficient budget".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: NFU vice-president Robyn Munt said: "The rapid uptake of the scheme comes as no surprise.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Its closure in less than six hours shows the scale of demand there is from farmers to deliver for the environment and to invest in farm resilience.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "The current cashflow pressures facing farmers and growers only exacerbates that demand as they look for certainty and clarity for the year ahead." Vicki Hird, agriculture lead at the Wildlife Trusts said "the scramble for green farming schemes was worse than the dash for Oasis tickets".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: When the scheme was suddenly closed without notice last year, there were concerns that some farmers might turn their backs on environmental work if they could not access the payments and demand for Tuesday's scheme was expected to be high.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The Nature Friendly Farming Network (NFFN), which helps farmers to manage land in environmentally-friendly ways, criticised the "frantic scramble" and said farmers had "faced a desperate race against time" to secure their funding agreements.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Cambridgeshire arable farmer Martin Lines, who leads the NFFN, said: "This entire SFI system, with windows opening and closing within a few hours, isn't fit for purpose.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "We need to find a better way based on continuous, whole-farm agreements, not doors that slam shut on day one because the money has already gone." He pointed out that after years of extreme weather, many farmers were relying on the funding to help adapt their farms to climate change and become more resilient.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said it would provide further information on future opportunities for funding applications in 2027 "soon".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: A Defra spokesperson said: "This year we ensured small farms and those new to SFI were prioritised - with an exclusive first window in the summer.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "This is a scheme that works for farmers, backs food production, and delivers practical, sustainable land management, supporting the aims of our farming roadmap, our long-term plan for English farming," he said.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Nicola Irvine and Toby White have been reporting an oily substance bubbling up in the river for more than a year An oil-like substance has been bubbling up in the River Avon in Bristol for years and killing wildlife, according to local residents who have made regular reports to the Environment Agency (EA).
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Nicola Irvine, who lives in Crews Hole, said it had been like "pulling teeth" getting the EA to investigate the pollution since she contacted them in July 2025.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Her partner, Toby White, said: "It's hard to describe how bad the smell is - at times it's like you're living on a petrol station and you start getting headaches." The EA said it had already visited the site and was "continuing to investigate the source of contamination and its damage to the environment".
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: An EA spokesperson added: "While minor impacts have been found where the contamination has entered the watercourse, we have not found wider environmental effects downstream.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Irvine said she first noticed the oily substance leaving a rainbow film on the river's surface and a strong acrid smell in early 2025.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: She reported it to the EA in July that year when she believed it was bubbling up rather than coming from boats.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: The EA first dismissed the substance as surface run-off but, after Irvine continued sending photos, including of dead wildlife, the investigation reopened in May this year.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "This stretch of the Avon used to regularly have 30 to 40 ducks, but now it's unusual to see more than a handful," she said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "I have personally found dead fish, ducks and ducklings.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Irvine said the issue had been even worse during this summer's heatwaves, which had led to her being prescribed medication for migraines.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "It would all bubble up, the smell would be so strong, it would surround the whole house," she said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: The EA said the pollution was a category three pollution incident because impacts were limited to the area where contamination enters the watercourse.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "I cant believe that even with all the health concerns and the fact there are otters in this river as well, it's still deemed minor," Irvine said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: In 2022, a leaked internal EA report told staff to ignore lower-impact category three and four pollution reports because of limited funding to investigate.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "I've been so frustrated with the EA," Irvine said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "It feels like pulling teeth trying to get any action from them." The EA is also investigating another incident nearby at Brislington Brook , where dead fish and eels, foam on the water and "an intense chemical smell" were reported by volunteers.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: The oily substance on the River Avon's surface in August 2025 Dominic Linnell, who walks his dog along the river every day, said he first noticed the issue more than two years ago.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "Two or three times a week, there's an awful chemical smell, and I see a huge oil slick that seems to bubble up from the bottom of the river," he said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "I've seen fish floating dead and ducks.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: There's a lot of wildlife along there, you get herons, so it's a real shame.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "We all really care about the river, it's definitely killing wildlife and it's very unpleasant," he said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Another local resident, Tristan Dhalla, said he had noticed the pollution ever since he moved to the area five years ago, and neighbours had even claimed the problem went back as far as a decade.

sentences.text: Wessex Water said their investigation had found "no issues" with any of their assets, while the substance did not pass through their sewerage network.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: A Bristol City Council spokesperson said it was supporting the EA's investigation by providing information and records, while officers had visited the site last week.

sentences.text: Longhorn cattle graze at a former open-cast coal mine on the edge of Salford People should not have to travel far to experience the joys of nature, conservationists have said, as campaigners push for more wildlife-rich green spaces in urban areas.

sentences.text: OpenAI has been at the centre of new concerns over uncontrolled AI activity OpenAI has acknowledged that it alerted "dozens" of global institutions that their websites may have been meddled with by its AI bots acting improperly.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: AI agents attempted to get information from "governments, universities, public agencies, and other institutions", including the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Census Bureau and Education Department, the company said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: The disclosures come days after Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that OpenAI agents had breached non-public files on the website of its government-run health care scheme.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Since August, public fears have grown over the potentially serious, even life-threatening, impacts of AI tools falling outside of human control.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: OpenAI said that some of the data was accessed by AI agents, essentially bots that are designed and trained to operate somewhat autonomously, which were working to find "authoritative sources of public information".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: But the company noted that some of the bots went beyond that and worked to bypass security measures on websites.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: When attempting to get information from the Census Bureau, for instance, AI agents used tools reserved for software developers to access it, the company said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: OpenAI said all of the government data accessed by bots was public.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: However, it noted that information that its bots accessed from the SEC, which regulates the US stock market and protects investors, was later published by AI agents on another website.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: OpenAI says this action was not intended.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: In other instances that OpenAI disclosed on Friday, its AI agents transferred data when it should not have.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Such activity resulted in at least 53 incidents where an OpenAI agent took an image from ChatGPT user activity and transferred it elsewhere.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: The company said that in each instance of a user image being used and transferred by an AI agent, the user had opted in to allow OpenAI to train models using their data.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Nevertheless, OpenAI admitted: "This is not an appropriate use of this data." It added that the leak of user images occurred before it had put in place new safeguards on AI training, and it was working to get all the user images transferred to any third-party removed.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Reuters first reported the expanded investigations.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: OpenAI also published details to its public blog.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: In certain instances of the agent activity, OpenAI said the tools "bypassed" security controls of some websites.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: In other instances, the AI agents showed "misalignment" in attempts to get at information from websites.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Misalignment is a term used by AI companies and researchers to describe instances where an AI tool did something that it was not trained to do or was otherwise unintended.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: OpenAI said that it was limiting identifying what entities were impacted because many had asked the company to not disclose details.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: "Our goal is to give each organization the facts and defer to them on if and when to make the incident public," it said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Not all of the instances involved in this incident were being considered a significant security breach, the company noted.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: "Some organizations may review what we share and conclude that the information was intentionally public or that the model's interaction was not concerning," it explained.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: "Others may identify a design issue or security weakness they want to address." Why are there concerns AI could threaten humanity, and how real are they?
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Could AI wipe out humans and how might it do it?
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: The company said many of the incidents are being referred to as "agent spam", which it described as "unexpected or concerning" AI agent activity, like posting information to the internet.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: OpenAI began taking such incidents more seriously after an incident in July where a group, or "swarm," of its AI agents hacked the AI developer platform Hugging Face without being prompted to do so.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Hugging Face was first to go public with the incident, with OpenAI publicly taking responsibility for it later.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: During that same UN meeting, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Dario Amodei, the head of rival firm Anthropic, asked for international leaders to form global standards for AI safety and ways to monitor and report such incidents.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: OpenAI said on Friday that it is currently reviewing training activity by its AI agents and going back on a "month by month" basis from when the Hugging Face hack occurred.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: "Most cases identified so far have been low severity, with limited or no evidence of meaningful impact," the company said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: He called for "an immediate, indefinite, international moratorium" on AI development.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: "We have yet to understand the extent of existing incidents, and future rogue AI scenarios could be catastrophic," Krueger said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Are we back in big tech's 'move fast and break things' era?
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites
