sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Take a look at clips from Silent Hill: Townfall As I creep through the heavy fog of Silent Hill: Townfall, I'm met by an oddly familiar sight amid the terror - a sign for a Sunday roast.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: For the first time, one of gaming's biggest horror franchises - created in Japan but traditionally set in the US - has come to the UK, set on a fictional Scottish island.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Jon McKellan, director at Glaswegian developers Screen Burn, told me taking on the mega brand was an "absolutely terrifying" prospect for the relatively small team.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: As a fan of the games, I was keen to find out what one of the most iconic survival horror series looks like in Scotland - and whether it can live up to its legacy.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Sadly there's no option to go inside The Mariner, have a nice cold pint, and wait for all this to blow over I played Silent Hill: Townfall, which was released on Thursday, on my PlayStation 5, and it ran well, though there have been some reports , external from others of performance issues.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Set in 1996, the game follows the plight of an American man called Simon Ordell, who washes up on St Amelia with a red hospital ID band around his wrist and an IV drip in his arm.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: As is to be expected from the Silent Hill games, the real reasons why you're there and what's going on are teased as you progress through the story in a typically vague fashion.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Simon Ordell arrives on the island of St Amelia, with no memory of who he is or why he's there The team took inspiration for the setting from the tiny fishing village of St Monans in Fife.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: For those concerned the game might lean into any typical Scottish stereotypes, McKellan told me he wanted it to feel "authentic and natural".
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: "It's not tartan everywhere, but if you grew up in a working-class town in the 90s, you will get a lot of the references," he said.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: In Townfall I walked past film-quality models of red pillar boxes, 20 mph speed limit signs and charity collection boxes shaped like guide dogs.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Not since 2006, when I had to storm Manchester Cathedral in Resistance: Fall of Man, have I felt an oddly patriotic attachment to game areas or objects.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: To save the game, I had to use a phone, which often meant stepping inside a "coins and card" telephone box - a sight instantly familiar to anyone old enough to remember them on British streets.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Meanwhile, a level set in a council estate leans into the concrete starkness of the area's looming grey buildings.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: While some may question why the main character is American rather than Scottish given the setting, there are narrative reasons why Simon is more of an outsider to this community, which are slowly drip-fed into cutscenes and in-game documents.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: For the most part I was intrigued by the story, which, like many of the previous games, explores themes of trauma and guilt sensitively.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: This edition also touches on ideas around the impact of big corporations on small communities, which brought added relevance to the setting of an isolated seaside town.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Even everyday objects like electricity meters appear as part of the game's puzzles and missions I soon had to face the island's monsters - gnarled, fleshy beings with axe-like heads or mangled faces.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: While St Amelia's inhabitants might not quite live up to the heights of Silent Hill 2's mannequins for sudden frights, their speed and general nastiness were still enough to make me want to run away as fast as possible.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Even when I picked up weapons such as a plank of wood or a steel pipe, a series staple, there was never much sense that I had the upper hand.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: These all degrade over time, and though I did eventually get a gun, bullets are scarce, meaning I still had to sneak around rather than face threats head-on.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: If you do end up going the wrong way down a one-way street, the game has a few weapons you can use, like this plank "We don't do jump scares, really," said McKellan - although I can think of a few alarming times playing the game I vehemently disagreed with that statement.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: The fear is dialled up an extra notch by Byron Bullock's rich sound design, with the music swelling almost unbearably intensely when spluttering nasties stumbled closer.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Composer Pilotpriest, also known as Anthony Scott Burns, deserves recognition too for his hauntingly bleak soundtrack.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: I think it says a lot that I closed every door I opened behind me in the game, in the naive hope it might stop monsters following - even at moments when there were none around.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: The CRT monitor is just one example of the retro tech used to avoid getting attacked Simon soon picks up a handheld CRT device to help with sneaking - a clever updated version of another staple of the Silent Hill series: the crackling radio.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: This piece of retro tech - basically a small portable TV - gives you a fuzzy image of nearby monsters on its screen, so you have some idea of where they are in order to avoid them, though it can get a little fiddly if there are several nearby.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: "I think it lends itself well to horror when the technology is a bit frail, a bit outdated," said McKellan.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: "You don't feel safe when those kinds of things are fragile." Later sections where you rely on even cruder tech to spot enemies ratchet up the tension further, at the expense of making the gameplay much slower.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Thankfully, there are often other cues as to the whereabouts of your fleshy foes, such as flickering lights and their awful, gurgling cries.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Reviews of the game have championed its atmosphere, with IGN's Tristan Ogilvie calling it "oppressively ominous".
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Silent Hill: Townfall has three difficulty settings for combat - easy, normal and nightmare (there are also two settings for puzzles, with one giving more hints).
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: I played on normal, though there were one or two sections with a new, super-strong and fast single enemy where I considered changing to easy.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: These were the most aggravating parts of the game for me, despite having played and loved Alien: Isolation, a game McKellan also worked on, which has a lot of challenging bits where you have to avoid the powerful Alien.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Chris Scullion, deputy editor at Video Games Chronicle said these moments were "deeply frustrating" and caused the game, which he otherwise found "outstanding", to come "grinding to a halt".
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Unfortunately for Simon, 20 is rarely plenty for the monsters of St Amelia Townfall is not the first time the series has strayed away from the original game's location in America, 2025's Silent Hill f was set in 1960s rural Japan.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: This sparked a conversation about whether a game can be part of the series yet not be set in or around the fictional eponymous town.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: The series' lead producer at Konami Motoi Okamoto told me the team were looking at various areas to potentially set the next games, from "other parts of Europe" to "Latin America".
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Games journalist and self-proclaimed "Silent Hillian" Vikki Blake told me the latest game exceeded her expectations, though she's still not convinced these newer games truly fit under the Silent Hill name.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: After my playthrough, I can see why Konami are pushing ahead with the idea to let other studios breathe new life into the franchise and take it to different destinations.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Townfall is a brutal, grim journey - uneven in parts, but clever - and full of immense tension and inventive game design, the kind that is needed to push a nearly 30-year-old franchise forward.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Okamoto has also expressed his desire , external to release a Silent Hill game every year - whether that be a remaster, remake, or entirely new material.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: If more new studios can keep the games feeling as fresh as this, we may eventually become like one of the series' many troubled protagonists – forgetting why we ever needed the titular town at all.
sentences.article_title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover

sentences.text: Current and former FBI agents have spoken to BBC News of their shock, fear and anger following a hack that appears to have exposed the private and personal information of the agency's entire workforce.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: "This is really bad for our undercover agents," says one former FBI agent, who fears for the safety of his colleagues.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The former cyber investigator is in a group chat with current agents who are worried their personal information could soon be freely available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: He says staff fear they could be targeted, or that criminals could use the data to create highly convincing phishing attempts, scams or demands for bribes.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The hacking group ShinyHunters is threatening to publish the stolen databases and documents within four days unless its demands are met.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: Some agents are also concerned about the risk of physical attacks from cyber criminals they have investigated.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: "One of the things we are discussing in the group chat is 'violence-as-a-service' attacks from young online gangs," says the former worker .
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: "They could use this information to harass an FBI agent who has worked on their cases." Groups similar to ShinyHunters - believed to be an English-speaking gang - have in the past been linked to swatting incidents, and even petrol bomb attacks against law enforcement officers and rivals.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: Swatting is a phenomenon so-called because perpetrators make calls that prompt armed police units - called Swat teams in the US - to swoop in on victims.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The group claims it breached FBI systems on Monday and later posted details of the attack on its darknet site.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The FBI has not responded to requests for comment.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: However, on Wednesday the agency acknowledged the breach - saying it was "aggressively investigating" how it occurred.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: For Michael McPherson, a former FBI agent who is now senior vice president of security operations at cyber firm ReliaQuest, the hack presents "a security threat which cuts to the core of agent safety, particularly their families".
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: He says agents understand the "inherent risks" that come with the job.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: "But this incident reportedly includes personal data such as home addresses and contact information, which could expose family members who are normally insulated from the threats associated with such a career," McPherson says.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: ShinyHunters shared samples of the alleged stolen data with reporters, along with an extortion demand.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The samples appear genuine and include names, addresses, phone numbers, badge numbers, job titles and information about spouses.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The records appear to relate to thousands of agents, including senior officials such as deputy directors.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The criminals also appear to possess highly sensitive medical information relating to thousands of special agents.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: BBC News has seen samples of stolen "fitness-for-work" medical examinations containing information such as blood and urine test results , along with doctors' notes mentioning conditions including a "shellfish and banana allergy".
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: Agents' full names and addresses, as well as references to medical issues including "blood in the urine" and "high cholesterol" are now in the criminals' hands.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: Cynthia Kaiser, who was the Deputy Director of Cyber at the FBI and now leads the Research Centre at Halcyon says ShinyHunters appear to already have lost control of some of the data which is circulating in various online groups of cyber researchers and could lead to harm even before the main tranche is published.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: "A lot of the damage may already be done, and as we have seen in past FBI data breaches, that information continues to circulate the dark web years later," she said.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: There are also concerns about the breach's national security implications, such as staff becoming targets for recruitment efforts by hostile foreign intelligence services.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: Alongside fear, many of those who spoke to the BBC expressed anger at the FBI for allowing the data to be stolen.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The hack is particularly embarrassing from a technical perspective because ShinyHunters is not generally regarded as a highly sophisticated hacking group.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: One former cyber agent said FBI staff were furious about the "sloppy and lazy security failures" that allegedly enabled the breach.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: There is also confusion about how to handle any fallout if data is published next week, as threatened.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The FBI appears unlikely to comply with the extortion demands, and the hackers have indicated they intend to post the information on their darknet site.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: Unusually, the group is not demanding money.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: Instead, it wants the FBI to retract an advisory published in May, which it claims "offended" them.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: "The agency leadership is lost," the former cyber investigator tells me.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: He says staff have been advised to sign up to a service called DeleteMe, which helps remove personal information from data broker websites - a response he feels is inadequate.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: The hack may raise further questions for FBI director Kash Patel, whose leadership has already faced scrutiny According to another former agent, there is widespread shock that such a breach could happen at one of the world's best-resourced law enforcement agencies.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: "You would think this information would not be internet-exposed.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: It's disturbing, actually," he says.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: There is also embarrassment that a prolific group of young cyber criminals has repeatedly managed to evade law enforcement while carrying out a string of high-profile hacks.
sentences.article_title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach

sentences.text: Egyptian sculptures are among the collection at the British Museum in London Overseas visitors will not be charged to enter England's national museums after ministers decided against changing the universal free admission policy.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: It comes after months of discussions between the government, museums, the tourism sector and local leaders to examine whether making tourists from abroad pay could boost the institutions' finances.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: In March, the government said it would explore charging international visitors to enter national museums as it looks for ways to tackle funding pressures.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: But the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) has now said this could deter domestic visitors and that any benefits of charging would not be felt equally across the sector.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: The UK's 15 national museums, including 12 in London, have been free for all to enter since 2001.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: But a review published last year by former Labour minister Baroness Margaret Hodge suggested that a charging model for international tourists "would align the UK with other countries, such as New Zealand and Singapore".
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: On Tuesday, DCMS confirmed free admission to these museums would remain in place for everyone.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: "The government believes that charging overseas visitors could deter domestic visitors and that the impacts and benefits of charging would not be felt equally across the sector and therefore will not introduce charges for overseas visitors," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: Culture secretary Lisa Nandy said: "Our museums are the places that light up the world.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: "That's why they must be free, forever, for everyone to access." The DCMS said national museums contribute more than £1bn a year to the economy and attract visitors from around the world, with the Natural History Museum and the British Museum drawing 7.1 million and 6.4 million visitors respectively in 2025.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: The Natural History Museum's director Dr Doug Gurr said although his museum would have benefitted from charging, the sector would have lost out overall.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: "Free museums aren't a cost to the economy - they're a key reason the economy benefits from tourism in the first place," he said.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: "So, we are delighted by the government's announcement that free entry for all will be maintained.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: "This will allow everyone to enjoy and have access to our great museums across the nation as one of the things this country does so brilliantly." The government also pointed to £760m in funding for museums through its £1.5bn Arts Everywhere Fund, as well as £600m in infrastructure funding for national museums.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: It said the £13.6m museum transformation programme would help organisations move towards more sustainable business models, while ministers would work with the Arts Council and the sector on a long-term strategic plan for museums, with further details to be announced.
sentences.article_title: National museums to stay free for all visitors

sentences.text: Luke Kennard attended Holyrood Academy in Chard An author whose latest book has been nominated for the prestigious Booker Prize said childhood boredom inspired his creativity.
sentences.article_title: Booker Prize nominee praises his school teachers

sentences.text: Luke Kennard, who grew up in Chard in Somerset, has been shortlisted for Black Bag , which is based on an experiment involving an actor sitting in a bin bag at the back of a lecture hall.
sentences.article_title: Booker Prize nominee praises his school teachers

sentences.text: He said, as a child, he had "quite a lot of time to practice" his creative passions.
sentences.article_title: Booker Prize nominee praises his school teachers

sentences.text: "You stay in your room playing the clarinet or writing a poem - there's a certain virtue to being a little bit bored sometimes, and just having to amuse yourself." Kennard attended Holyrood Academy from 1992 to 1999 and studied both GCSE and A-level English Literature.
sentences.article_title: Booker Prize nominee praises his school teachers

sentences.text: He added: "It was the teachers that I had who really encouraged my writing- that's quite foundational." Kennard said the former head of English, Paul Coffman, would read his short stories during break times, and leave him notes and suggestions.
sentences.article_title: Booker Prize nominee praises his school teachers

sentences.text: "He was the first person who really got me to take my writing seriously." Luke Kennard says his teachers supported his writing Holyrood Academy said it was "thrilled" with Kennard's nomination.
sentences.article_title: Booker Prize nominee praises his school teachers

sentences.text: It added his praise of Coffman "is a moving reminder of the lasting impact teachers can have on the lives and achievements of their students".
sentences.article_title: Booker Prize nominee praises his school teachers

sentences.text: "This remarkable accomplishment is a testament to Luke's talent, dedication and love of literature.
sentences.article_title: Booker Prize nominee praises his school teachers

sentences.text: "We couldn't be prouder." The winner of the 2026 Booker Prize will be announced on 9 November.

sentences.text: It may also ban you from re-entering the site.

sentences.article_title: Mistakes to avoid when buying Glastonbury tickets

sentences.text: The sculptures have been on display in the British Museum since the 19th Century, though Greece has long disputed the legality of their removal.

sentences.text: Mitsotakis and his government have previously held talks with the British Museum about the sculptures, but the two have so far failed to reach an agreement, with Greek authorities seeking their permanent return.

sentences.text: Instead, he urged Burnham to stand by his previous comments on the sculptures and find a way of returning them for good.
sentences.article_title: Greek PM urges Burnham to return Elgin Marbles permanently

sentences.text: This would be a "decisive step", Mitsotakis said, that would "reunite the sculptures and transform a historic dispute into a unique act of cultural friendship".

sentences.text: Usman Muhammad survived but 33 others died in the cell and four others died later in hospital Usman Muhammad pauses by the entrance to a tiny Nigerian prison cell and leans his forehead against the wall unable to speak.

sentences.text: "I have never felt heat like that in my life.
sentences.article_title: 'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria

sentences.article_title: 'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria

sentences.article_title: 'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria

sentences.text: Nigeria's men failed to qualify for both the 2022 and 2026 Fifa World Cups As Nigeria begin their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign, former international Segun Odegbami, who won the tournament on home soil in 1980, says the country is experiencing the "worst time" in its football history.

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Odegbami says the diminishing returns represent a "tectonic shift" for one of the continent's traditional powers.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "It has never been this bad in our entire history that we didn't qualify for the World Cup," the 74-year-old told BBC Sport Africa.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "Our girls (the Super Falcons), who were African champions, failed to win a competition (the 2025 Women's Afcon) that was just there for their taking.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: All our junior teams are not doing well.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "Our local league is not bringing in money.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Something is definitely wrong." The crisis has already triggered major changes within the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF).
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Its president Ibrahim Gusau, general secretary Mohammed Sanusi and multiple members of the federation's executive committee resigned last month following mounting criticism.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Odegbami says Nigerian football had not been represented by its "first XI administrators" and has called for a restructure to create the conditions for long-term development.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "The outcry by Nigerians was total.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Everybody wanted them out, to the extent that the President of the country himself (Bola Tinubu) made the pronouncement that he wanted reforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: The parties are working towards a roadmap for comprehensive reforms but NFF elections, scheduled for 27 September, have been suspended.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: President Tinubu stated his desire for reform to overcome what he called "repeated failures".
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Emmanuel Ikpeme has been appointed NFF interim general secretary, with Ademola Olajire the interim deputy general secretary.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Nigerian sports journalist Fisayo Dairo believes any reform must extend beyond a change in leadership.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "The reform should be the setting up of a proper framework and structure that our football can thrive on," Dairo told BBC Sport Africa.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "[We need to] develop national teams, harness talent from the grassroots and have governance that incorporates all forms of stakeholders.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Nicknamed 'Mathematical' for his precision and skill on the ball, the forward was part of the Super Eagles side that won the country's first continental title in 1980, beating Algeria 3-0 in the final in Lagos.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "We had unprecedented support and fortunately the stars aligned with us," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "It was an indescribable atmosphere during that period.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "That experience you can't even describe and compare. [It remains] indelible in our minds." Nigeria lifted the Afcon trophy again in 1994 and 2013, and finished as runners-up at the 2023 edition.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: The team also finished third in 2019 and at this year's finals in Morocco.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: However, Odegbami argues sport has "not been a priority" of successive governments and believes his nation has been failed by football administrators since the mid 1990s.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "The pilots are not guiding us well, they haven't guided us well," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "And that has affected every aspect of our football development: the grassroots, the discovery of players, the development of the players, the establishment of the institutions that will take care of them, the academies, the clubs that they will go into both locally and internationally.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "What is the coaching methodology?

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Odegbami has bemoaned the fact that top-class stadiums which Nigeria used to possess have fallen into disrepair after being neglected.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: He name-checked the National Stadium in Surulere, Lagos, which hosted games during the 1980 and 2000 Afcons, the Liberty Stadium (now Obafemi Awolowo Stadium) in Ibadan, Kaduna's Ahmadu Bello Stadium and the UJ Esuene Stadium in Calabar.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "I weep when I think of the amount of damage they have done to Nigerian football - the infrastructure that we had in the country, some of the historic monuments that were facilities for football in this country," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "Whether it was wilful, whether it was ignorance, they did irreparable damage to what was Nigeria's heritage.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "Uyo is the best we have in Nigeria, but it is not half as good as what we had from the 1960s to the 90s." sentences.text: Tatjana Smith was the only South African to win a gold medal at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris Having ended a two-year exile from competitive swimming, South Africa's most successful Olympian Tatjana Smith has revealed she "lost the love" for her sport before stepping away from the pool in 2024.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The 29-year-old's decision to retire straight after the Paris Games came as a surprise, given she had just won 200m breaststroke gold in the French capital to add to her 100m title from Tokyo 2020.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: But after two years away, which included several months in which she did not swim at all, Smith says she is now "free from the things that made me hate swimming".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "My whole life, I was kind of a robot towards swimming," she told Newsday on the BBC World Service.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "You're so zoned in, you're obsessed with something, so there isn't actually time for you to think about things outside of the pool that you potentially have a passion for.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think probably everyone would think that the timing [of retirement] was the worst.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Smith on retirement and becoming South Africa’s most decorated Olympian But despite making history for her country, Smith says financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, also contributed to her decision to retire.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The financial burden on any athlete is so tough," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I relied on my parents funding me until I broke the world record at the Olympics.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: And then, all of a sudden, now people are interested in maybe sponsoring you.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "But the majority of sponsorships for athletes are based on performance.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: So then you have that pressure and expectation to always have to perform, otherwise you're not going to get paid.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think the financial side, and also being in a system where they're not really putting the athletes first, made it really difficult." Smith won her first Olympic title under her maiden name Schoenmaker, before changing her surname when she married sports agent Joel Smith in 2023.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The marriage made her part of a wider South African sporting dynasty, given that her sister-in-law is Rachel Smith, who was married to Springboks captain Siya Kolisi before their split.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Tatjana Smith admits her own marriage changed the way she thought about her future.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Thinking about families as a woman, you have to time it perfectly, because if you're pregnant, it's not like you can still compete." While children are not yet part of her journey, Smith says working out what to do next was far from easy.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I definitely understand what athletes mean from the post-Olympic depression," said the 2023 200m breaststroke world champion, who also counts Commonwealth and African titles among her achievements.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "It was such an emptiness in my life, because my whole life revolved around swimming.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I don't have to eat at a certain time, I don't have to sleep at a certain time, I don't have to think about travelling or not spending time with family anymore.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The world is so overwhelming.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's like, in which direction to go?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "It was definitely the toughest season that I had to go through.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: I think it's probably why it's made me a stronger person." Smith married her husband Joel in November 2023 and says family life was one of the reasons behind her decision to retire Initially, Smith took on speaking engagements to pay the bills.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: She smiles when she admits: "I hate public speaking.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: I hate being in front of people." The same cannot be said of her love for competition.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Having returned to the pool in order to keep fit, she decided to have a crack at triathlon, something she describes as a "crazy idea".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The training was so intense, and I was like, 'OK, I might as well just go back to swimming if I'm going to train this hard'," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Every time I went back to the swimming pool and I dived in, I was like, 'Yeah, this is a feeling that I really miss so much'.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think slowly over the year and a half, I just realised 'Wow, I really do love swimming'." Having made her decision to come out of retirement, Smith now wants to freshen things up and "try something new".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: That means a change to the 50m breaststroke, an event which has just been added to the Olympic schedule for the first time ahead of the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I thought, 'Why don't I try?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Why don't I give myself that challenge?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Reinvent myself'," said Smith.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I always try and describe it to someone that maybe doesn't understand swimming; it's like a 400m runner and a 100m [runner].
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's two different body types, two different trainings, and that's where I'm going." It means she has more than halved her training volume, with three sessions a week instead of eight - a change she believes will help her retain her love for her sport and live a more balanced life.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I feel like I'm being so lazy because I used to do 12km per day and now the focus is on taking time to be as explosive as possible.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Now I'm doing 12km over a whole week.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I have 20 years of endurance in my pocket, but I can definitely see I don't have those fast twitch [muscle] fibres.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's a whole different way of teaching my body how to swim." Those initial 20 years in the pool left Smith feeling burned out.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Now she says she has earned the right to do things on her terms.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Swimming was an opportunity given to me by my parents and I believe I took it on full heartedly.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "But, for the first time, it's my decision whether I want to come back.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I've achieved way more than I ever dreamed in my whole life, so I have nothing to prove." BBC African Sports Personality of the Year 2021: Tatjana Schoenmaker profile.

sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: The gift, which was unveiled before VIP guests at the Thursday dinner, embodies "the free and soaring spirit of America", said Trump .
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: He said that he and First Lady Melania Trump participated in its design.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: The statue is part of a valuable - but sometimes tricky - aspect of international diplomacy: gift-giving.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: Such gifts are a small but meaningful element of the larger aim of Xi and Trump's three-day summit – forging personal relationships between heads of two global superpowers.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: "They're going to discuss all of these complicated issues," Daniel Kritenbrink, partner at The Asia Group says.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: "But at the end of the day, these are still two human beings.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: "So that personal relationship means something," he says.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: "I think the gift exchange is one key part of that." Kritenbrink, who spent over 30 years as a US diplomat, mostly in Asia, says personal relationships are of particular importance to Xi.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: He believes the direct Trump-Xi bond is the glue that is holding together "the most complex and the most consequential relationship in the world".

sentences.text: He says Trump, too, values what Kritenbrink calls "leader-level diplomacy".

sentences.text: Today, the practice of giving lavish gifts mostly exists in Gulf states and autocratic governments.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: "Autocracies like China give much more expensive gifts," says Morten Skumsrud Andersen, who co-authored a study on diplomacy and gifts with Sending.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: In the West, Andersen says, the tradition has been watered down by democratic guardrails and restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: For example, the US Constitution has an emoluments clause that puts a dollar-value limit on gifts a president can receive from a foreign government.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: Currently, the limit is $525 (£397).
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: Anything higher and it becomes federal property, unless the president chooses to buy it back with his own money.
sentences.article_title: Why Trump gave Xi an ornate bald eagle statue at the state dinner

sentences.text: Also, when giving a gift beyond a certain amount, a US president would have to go through Congress, unless he was paying for it personally.

sentences.text: Anderson adds: "This is not a last-minute purchase at the airport." The bald eagle has become an American icon During Xi's state visit to the US in 2013, then-President Barack Obama gifted him an inscribed bench made of redwood, native to California where the two had met.

sentences.text: Padma Chamchot, Tsering Yangdol, Tsering Dolker and Palzes Angmo (left to right) - Hanle's astro-ambassadors, trained to guide visitors through the night sky It's 10pm and bitterly cold in Hanle.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Strong winds sweep across this remote village in India's Himalayan Ladakh region, but no one seems to mind.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Dinner is over, yet, instead of bed, many people are gathering outside.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The reason is above them.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: At 14,764ft (4,500m) above sea level, Hanle is known for its exceptionally clear, dark skies .
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Wrapped in thick jackets, woollen caps and gloves, tourists and visitors gather to see the Milky Way and look through telescopes at planets, the Moon and distant stars.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Among them are four young women: Palzes Angmo, Tsering Dolker, Tsering Yangdol and Padma Chamchot.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: They are Hanle's astro-ambassadors, trained to guide visitors through the night sky.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: By day, they cook meals, clean rooms and look after guests at their family-run homestays.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: By night, they set up telescopes, trace constellations with laser pointers and explain what visitors are seeing in the dark skies.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: These women - all in their late 20s - grew up watching these stars, but it was only a few years ago that they learnt to study them through a telescope.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "The sky here has always been twinkling like this," 28-year-old Dolker says.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The difference today is that people travel hundreds of kilometres to see what locals have long regarded as an ordinary part of life.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The Indian Astronomical Observatory is one of the world's highest sites for astronomical observation Hanle's remote, high-altitude location, dry air and lack of light pollution make its skies prized by astronomers.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The cold desert offers suitable observing conditions on around 260 nights a year.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Hanle is also home to the Indian Astronomical Observatory, run by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, and is a major centre for astronomical research.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: In 2022, it became India's first Dark Sky Reserve, helping protect its pristine skies from artificial light and putting Hanle on the astronomy tourism map.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Visitor numbers have since surged: from about 3,000 a year five years ago to nearly 30,000 in 2024-25, according to government figures.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: As visitors grew, so did opportunities for locals.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: In 2022, the Ladakh administration and Indian Institute of Astrophysics trained 24 young people from Hanle and nearby villages in astronomy.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: These four women were among them.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Over 15 days, they learnt to identify stars, planets and constellations, navigate the night sky, operate telescopes and photograph the Milky Way on their phones.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Becoming astronomy guides was never part of their plans.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: They were nervous when they first handled the equipment, fearing they might break something.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Gradually, they learnt how it worked and grew confident using it.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Hanle was designated as India's first dark sky reserve in 2022 Four years on, they are confident astronomers, with evenings beginning around 9pm.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: They position telescopes for the night's planets and constellations before guiding visitors from local homestays.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: They show them the Moon's craters, Saturn's rings, Vega - the brightest star in the night sky - and other planets, using laser pointers to trace constellations and objects visible to the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Then comes the Milky Way.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: At 11pm each night, the village switches off its lights, plunging Hanle into darkness as visitors scramble to photograph the now-brilliant galaxy.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "When people look through the telescope and capture a photo alongside the Milky Way, they experience immense joy.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: We also help them with their mobile phone settings so they can capture the Milky Way," Padma Chamchot says.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: It often starts with helping one visitor take a picture and ends with a long queue.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The women take pictures for their own social media too, comparing notes on the stars and other sights they captured that night.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The women also point laser at the sky to help visitors spot stars visible to the naked eye But by day, life is more ordinary.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Hanle has few hotels and no resorts, so visitors mostly stay in family-run homestays, often extensions of their homes.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Chamchot's family runs one too.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "Taking care of guests, cooking meals, cleaning rooms, and managing household chores fills our day," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "From nine in the evening, we begin setting up the telescopes for the night's stargazing sessions." Their families' homestays remain the main income source, but the women earn about 25,000 rupees ($260; £193) a month from astronomy, charging 200 rupees a session.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Income dips during the harsh winter, when few tourists visit, but the earnings have given them greater financial independence: they no longer need to ask their parents for money.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "We can save our earnings and spend them on things we want - including new phones," Padma says.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: For the astro-ambassadors, the transformation has been personal as much as financial.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "Before taking on this work, we lacked confidence," they say.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: However, the growing popularity of Hanle comes with risks.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The same tourism that supports local livelihoods could also threaten the darkness that makes Hanle unique.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Rapid construction and rising tourism also poses a threat to Hanle's dark skies Visitor numbers have surged, fuelled partly by social media posts about Hanle's night skies and its location on the route to Umling La, which is among the world's highest motorable mountain passes.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: But more tourists also mean more traffic, construction and artificial light - all threats to the darkness they come to see.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Sonam Jorphail, a senior engineer and head of outreach at the IAO, says tourism is creating jobs and driving development in Hanle, but growth must be managed to protect its dark skies.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "They bridge the gap between the science community and common people - locals and visitors," Jorphail adds.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: But longtime residents say Hanle's night sky is already changing.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Padma's father, Dhuntup Chamchot, in his 70s, remembers when the skies were even darker.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "Back then, when the weather was good, people would often sleep outdoors under the open sky," he says.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The young women often take their families stargazing too.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "We frequently show the night sky to our families through the telescope.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: They enjoy looking at it now," says Yangdol, one of the astro-ambassadors.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "If one of us takes even a single day off, the families ask why the telescope was not set up," she jokes.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The women say they have no desire to leave Hanle or its dark skies.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: They hope for advanced training and better telescopes and eyepieces to enhance visitors' experience.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Four years ago, the equipment was unfamiliar; now, they are building a future around the stars.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky
